title: PCA & autoencoders
blurb: Directions of max variance, bottleneck autoencoders and their variants

hook.title: Choosing the best shadow
hook.text: A 3-D sculpture casts a 2-D shadow. Rotate the lamp: from some angles the shadow shows almost everything about the shape, from others it collapses to a blob. **PCA** picks the lamp angle where the shadow is **widest** (max variance). An **autoencoder** learns its own way of casting a shadow (the encoder) *and* of rebuilding the sculpture from it (the decoder), squeezing everything through a narrow bottleneck.
hook.recall: Remember the shadow: widest shadow = most variance kept = least reconstruction error. A linear autoencoder with MSE finds roughly the same shadow as PCA.

explore.intro: 80 two-dimensional points; you choose the 1-D direction of the code.
tasks: Drag the angle. Where is the variance kept largest, and where is the reconstruction error smallest?
Press *Snap to PC1*. Does kept + lost ever change?
explore.takeaway: PCA: find directions of max variance, transform, keep the top few. Kept variance + lost variance = constant, so the widest shadow minimises reconstruction error.

build.prompt: Order the three PCA steps shown on the slides.
items: Find the directions of maximum variance
Transform the features into those directions
Keep only a subset of the directions with the most variance (dimensionality reduction)

questions.prompt: An MLP autoencoder with **no** non-linear activations trained with MSE is:
questions.explanation: Slide 16’s red note: without non-linearities and with MSE it is very similar to PCA (but the latent dimensions need not be orthogonal).

questions.prompt: The slide’s convolutional AE compresses $28\times28=784$ inputs to a 32-dimensional latent. What is the compression ratio $784/32$?
Which statement about autoencoder variants is FALSE?
options: Denoising AE: add dropout/noise to the input and learn to reconstruct the clean image
Sparse AE: add an $L_1$ penalty $\sum_i|Enc_i(x)|$ on the code
Dropout layers force the network to learn redundant features
Sparse AE adds an $L_2$ penalty on the decoder weights
questions.explanation: The sparsity penalty is $L_1$ on the **code**: $\mathcal L=\|x-Dec(Enc(x))\|_2^2+\sum_i|Enc_i(x)|$.

questions.prompt: *“In a linear autoencoder the latent dimensions are exactly the principal components: orthogonal and ordered by variance.”* What’s the problem?
options: The slide notes the latent dimensions are not necessarily orthogonal and will have roughly the same variance, unlike PCA components
questions.explanation: Same shadow *subspace*, but the AE doesn’t sort its axes the way PCA does.

questions.prompt: The reconstruction loss on the AE slide is:
questions.explanation: Squared error between input and reconstruction.
